Fastest gains: better titles and intros for pages at Google positions 8-16.
Evidence-led: cite PubMed for any claim; mark untested claims "not studied".

facts: African hair grew more slowly on average: about 3.7 vs 5.7 inches a year (PMIDs 11531795, 27019510; grouped by ethnicity, not curl type).
Tightly coiled hair knots in 10-16% of shafts vs 0.15% in other groups (PMID 11050586).
Coconut, olive and sunflower oil get into the hair shaft; mineral oil doesn't (PMIDs 11413497, 16258695). Coconut oil before washing reduced protein loss (PMID 12715094).
Traction alopecia: 31.7% of South African adult women, 17.1% of schoolgirls (PMID 18694677).
Scalp massage: 9 men, 4 min a day, thicker hair at 24 weeks, no control group (PMID 26904154).
No study compares curl creams or shows a cream reduces shrinkage. Aunt Jackie's Curl La La contains no flaxseed.
avoid: Invented stats, studies or percentages (e.g. shrinkage %, "protective styles cut friction 50-60%"). No source, no number.
Saying jojoba, almond or avocado oil penetrates hair: not shown (only coconut, olive, sunflower; see facts).
Saying peppermint oil grows hair in people: shown in mice only (PMID 25584150).
"Scalp massage boosts blood flow 69%": no source exists (removed Nov 7).
Saying 4C hair grows "half an inch a month" like other hair: in studies it grew slower (see facts).
Saying a study sets protein treatment frequency: none does.
Star ratings, review counts, Amazon prices, bestseller claims; saying Strand tested products.
Cure, growth-guarantee or health claims; in Meta ads, "you/your hair" framing.
Promising any freebie other than the 4C Wash Day Checklist.
rules: Plain-words affiliate disclosure before the first Amazon link; Amazon tag strand01-20.
Palette: espresso #3D2B1F, caramel #C4945A, cream #FAF7F2; text on light backgrounds uses #8B5E1A.
Pins: 1000x1500, keyword in the first 40 characters of the title, straight apostrophes, footer hairtypequiz.hair.

pins: Every pin links to a post or the quiz; quiz pins by hair type earn the most clicks.
Titles up to 100 characters, keyword first; descriptions up to 500, no hashtag stuffing.
outline: Lead the title with the exact search phrase; meta 140-155 characters; answer the question in the first two sentences.
Plan a quiz link and 2-3 internal links.
factcheck: Check every number against Verified facts; anything else is unverified, with a PubMed search phrase to settle it.
compliance: FTC: disclosure before the first affiliate link. Amazon: the required statement is in every footer; no prices or ratings.
visual: The owner prefers Canva photographic pins: real natural hair, no before/after, warm light.
critique: Check the footer is spelled hairtypequiz.hair, look for AI flaws in hands and hair, and check headline readability at phone size.
custom: Strand is hairtypequiz.hair: a free hair type quiz (1A-4C) plus an evidence-led blog, paid by Amazon affiliate clicks.
